cli_subcommands.about: Parse and validate a Btor2 model and print its features as JSON
cli_subcommands.name: info

cli_subcommands.about: Print a Btor2 model in canonical form
cli_subcommands.name: fmt

cli_subcommands.about: Check one model with the engine portfolio
cli_subcommands.name: check

cli_subcommands.about: Load a model at bit level (AIGER, or Btor2 bit-blasted), preprocess it and print its size before and after; `--aag` prints the result
cli_subcommands.name: simp

cli_subcommands.about: Lower SystemVerilog to Btor2 with svlang; immediate assertions become bad states
cli_subcommands.name: lower

cli_subcommands.about: Run a JasperGold or VC Formal style Tcl script (or an interactive shell when no script is given)
cli_subcommands.name: shell

cli_subcommands.about: Serve one FPV session to an AI model as Model Context Protocol tools on standard input and output (docs/ai-interface.md). Replies are JSON; what the session prints goes to standard error
cli_subcommands.name: mcp

cli_subcommands.about: Shrink an AIGER model while two engines keep disagreeing on it, or while a test command keeps exiting 0 (delta debugging)
cli_subcommands.name: reduce

cli_subcommands.about: Prove a property whose bad output is an OR of several terms part by part: one model per term, proved a few at a time with the invariant store carrying each certified invariant to the others, then the original with all of them (see docs/engines.md)
cli_subcommands.name: split

cli_subcommands.about: Run engines over every model in a directory and log to the run database
cli_subcommands.name: bench

cli_subcommands.about: Generate or verify single-source-of-truth Markdown reference manuals, `docs/reference/index.json`, and `llms.txt` from CLI, Tcl, and MCP registries
cli_subcommands.name: docgen

arguments.description: Name of the failing (`cex`) property to triage (optional: defaults to first failing property)
arguments.name: property

mcp_prompts.description: Expert root-cause workflow: fuse causal slice + driver snippets via `cex_diagnose`, classify RTL bug vs missing input assumption vs broken SVA, validate any fix with `proposal_validate`, and optionally launch a visual walkthrough via `gui_present_cex`.
mcp_prompts.name: triage_cex
mcp_prompts.title: Triage a failing counterexample (CEX)

arguments.description: Name of the `undetermined` property to converge (optional: defaults to first undetermined property)
arguments.name: property

mcp_prompts.description: Structured convergence ladder for `undetermined` properties: inspect complexity/telemetry via `convergence_diagnose`, mine inductive helper invariants with `proposal_validate(kind="assert")`, or apply sound cutpoint/blackbox/case-split abstractions.
mcp_prompts.name: close_undetermined
mcp_prompts.title: Close an undetermined formal proof

arguments.description: Natural-language hardware specification requirement to formalize
arguments.name: requirement

arguments.description: Optional module/scope name (defaults to top module)
arguments.name: module

mcp_prompts.description: Spec-driven SVA engineering hydrated with the DUT's exact input/output port boundary: write reset-guarded safety assertions paired with non-vacuity witness covers and verify them via `proposal_validate` before proposing.
mcp_prompts.name: spec_to_sva
mcp_prompts.title: Synthesize verifiable SVA from a specification requirement

arguments.description: Optional path to `fvp.spec.json` (`informal.spec/1`); auto-discovered when omitted
arguments.name: spec_file

mcp_prompts.description: Run a complete signoff gate across the live session: `spec_audit` against `fvp.spec.json` (if present), `formal_lint`, assumption over-constraint/vacuity audit, `under_ai` provenance review, cover reachability, and `check_cov` COI/UNR coverage.
mcp_prompts.name: audit_signoff
mcp_prompts.title: Formal verification signoff & soundness audit

mcp_tools.description: Start the session over from a JasperGold or VC Formal Tcl script (`script`), or from SystemVerilog files with a top module, clock and reset (`files`). A script runs as written, including any prove in it. Returns the session summary; a script that stops with an error gives ok=false and the error, with the session as far as it got.
mcp_tools.name: session_open
mcp_tools.title: Open a design

mcp_tools.description: Report, per line, every command or option of a Tcl script that the tool would reject, ignore or does not know. Nothing is elaborated or proved and the open session is not touched.
mcp_tools.name: script_check
mcp_tools.title: Check a script without running it

mcp_tools.description: The design setup (top, files, clocks, reset, cut points), the engines, property counts by kind and status, and what an AI has added or proposed.
mcp_tools.name: session_summary
mcp_tools.title: Session summary

mcp_tools.description: The session's last console lines: notes and warnings from elaboration and proving, and every AI-added change.
mcp_tools.name: session_log
mcp_tools.title: Console log

mcp_tools.description: The assertions, assumptions and covers of the session with their status, optionally filtered.
mcp_tools.name: property_list
mcp_tools.title: List properties

mcp_tools.description: One property with its status, the engine and time that settled it, its source location and every engine's run.
mcp_tools.name: property_get
mcp_tools.title: One property

mcp_tools.description: The inputs and registers in a property's cone of influence, nearest first: distance is the number of register stages between the signal and the property.
mcp_tools.name: property_cone
mcp_tools.title: Signals a property depends on

mcp_tools.description: The instance tree of the elaborated design: each scope's module, ports and signals with widths.
mcp_tools.name: design_hierarchy
mcp_tools.title: Design hierarchy

mcp_tools.description: What the design holds, counted on its netlist (instances, inputs, flops, latches, memories, clocks and resets found), what the script declared (clocks, reset, black boxes, the current task's cut points and properties), and the size of the current task's model after lowering (Btor2 nodes, states, inputs, constraints, targets, and the bit-blasted AIG). Builds the model, so it takes as long as one lowering.
mcp_tools.name: design_info
mcp_tools.title: Design information

mcp_tools.description: Lines of a design file or script, by line range (at most 400 lines a call).
mcp_tools.name: design_source
mcp_tools.title: Source text

mcp_tools.description: The trace of a property whose status is cex or covered: one value per signal and frame (a frame is a clock cycle; frame 0 is the reset cycle). Words are in hex, single bits 0 or 1. hit_at lists the frames in which the assertion fails or the cover is hit. Without `signals`, the signals the property names come first, then the rest of its cone.
mcp_tools.name: trace_get
mcp_tools.title: Counterexample or cover trace as data

mcp_tools.description: Run the engines on the named assertions and covers (the enabled ones of the task, or of the current task, when none is named) and return each one's result. Each task is proved on its own model, with its own assumptions and cut points. Only this gives a verdict. With wait=false it returns at once: follow with prove_status, end with prove_stop.
mcp_tools.name: prove
mcp_tools.title: Prove properties

mcp_tools.description: Whether a prove is running, each property's state so far, and the result of the last prove started with wait=false once it has ended.
mcp_tools.name: prove_status
mcp_tools.title: Progress of a prove

mcp_tools.description: Ask a running prove to stop. Properties not settled yet become undetermined (stopped).
mcp_tools.name: prove_stop
mcp_tools.title: Stop a prove

mcp_tools.description: Zero-side-effect scratch-task soundness oracle: tests a candidate `assume`, helper `assert` (lemma), `cover`, or `cut_point` BEFORE calling `proposal_add`. Checks syntax, SV-FPV-001 DUT-output over-constraint hygiene, bounded environment consistency + UNSAT conflict core, 2QBF dead-end trap states, vacuity, cover non-regression (`lost_covers`), and whether target assertions become `proven`. Leaves the live session completely untouched.
mcp_tools.name: proposal_validate
mcp_tools.title: Validate a candidate assumption, helper assertion, cover, or cut point

mcp_tools.description: Propose an assumption, a helper assertion, a cover (`expr`, SystemVerilog in the top module's scope) or a cut point (`signal`). Call `proposal_validate` first to verify soundness, non-vacuity, and cover non-regression. In propose mode it waits for a person (state pending); in automatic mode it is applied at once, tagged AI-added.
mcp_tools.name: proposal_add
mcp_tools.title: Propose a change

mcp_tools.description: Every change proposed through this interface since the design was opened, with its state.
mcp_tools.name: proposal_list
mcp_tools.title: List proposals

mcp_tools.description: Take back one proposal (`id`) or all of them: a pending one is withdrawn, an applied one is removed from the session, and every result that was found with it in the model goes back to unprocessed (`reset`).
mcp_tools.name: proposal_undo
mcp_tools.title: Take back proposals

mcp_tools.description: Dynamic backward slice from a falsified assertion (`cex`) or reached cover (`covered`) at failure frame T back to frame 0: walks only active mux arms (`ite`), controlling boolean operands, and register state transitions, pruning untaken datapaths and idle hold cycles.
mcp_tools.name: why_cex
mcp_tools.title: Root-cause slice of a counterexample trace

mcp_tools.description: Preferred first tool for any `cex` or `covered` property: fuses `property_get`, backward `why_cex` causal slice, trimmed trace on active causal signals only, primary-input vs DUT-output/internal signal role classification, RTL driver source snippets (`signal_nav`), `formal_lint` findings, and a triage hint into one compact reply.
mcp_tools.name: cex_diagnose
mcp_tools.title: Single-call counterexample root-cause dossier

mcp_tools.description: Preferred first tool for `undetermined` or slow properties: fuses per-engine telemetry (`stats`, `max_bound`), COI input/register counts, `fv_complexity` arithmetic/memory/blackbox hotspots, active assumptions/cutpoints, and ranked proof-convergence tactics.
mcp_tools.name: convergence_diagnose
mcp_tools.title: Single-call proof convergence & complexity dossier

mcp_tools.description: Enable, disable, or inspect the cone-of-influence SHA-256 proof cache (`set_prove_cache*`).
mcp_tools.name: prove_cache
mcp_tools.title: Configure or inspect the COI proof cache

mcp_tools.description: Initialize, measure, query, or clear formal coverage (`coi`, `branch`, `toggle`, `functional`).
mcp_tools.name: check_cov
mcp_tools.title: Formal COI observability and UNR dead-code coverage

mcp_tools.description: Load a connectivity CSV map into the `Connectivity` task, prove its rules, list statuses, or clear it.
mcp_tools.name: check_conn
mcp_tools.title: Formal CSV connectivity verification

mcp_tools.description: Initialize, prove, list, or clear 2-copy self-composition X-propagation checks across outputs, control muxes, memories, assertions, or explicit signals.
mcp_tools.name: check_xprop
mcp_tools.title: Exact 2-copy formal X-propagation verification

mcp_tools.description: Create, prove, list, or clear 2-safety non-interference rules proving secret `-from` signals never influence observable `-to` signals.
mcp_tools.name: check_spv
mcp_tools.title: 2-safety formal security taint / non-interference verification

mcp_tools.description: Configure, prove, list, or clear dual-design equivalence checks between a reference `spec` RTL and a refactored/pipelined `imp` RTL (`lec: false` for sequential SEC with optional `latency`, `lec: true` for combinational keypoint LEC).
mcp_tools.name: check_sec
mcp_tools.title: Dual-design formal sequential (SEC) and combinational (LEC) equivalence checking

mcp_tools.description: Load an OpenTitan HJSON/JSON, CSV, or UVM RAL `.sv` (`uvm_reg_block`) register specification into task `CSR` and prove reset, read-back, `RW`/`RO`/`W1C`/`W1S`/`W0C`/`WO`/`RC` access, `regwen` lock, and address non-aliasing properties.
mcp_tools.name: check_csr
mcp_tools.title: Automated CSR / RAL formal register verification

mcp_tools.description: Generate, prove, list, or clear formal bus protocol assertion/assumption/cover VIP suites in task `Protocol` for TileLink-UL (`tlul`), AMBA AXI4-Lite (`axi4lite`), or AMBA APB (`apb`).
mcp_tools.name: check_protocol
mcp_tools.title: Formal bus protocol VIP SVA generator (`tlul`, `axi4lite`, `apb`)

mcp_tools.description: Open or refresh the interactive InFormal verification workbench (MCP App side pane or full-page view): property status table, waveform viewer, causal schematic, RTL source, and Formal Apps.
mcp_tools.name: open_workbench
mcp_tools.title: InFormal

mcp_tools.description: Extract a bounded, port-aware RTL netlist schematic subgraph in the cone of influence of `name`, annotated with active `why_cex` causal paths and arithmetic state-space hotspots (`mul`, `div`, wide datapath).
mcp_tools.name: schematic_get
mcp_tools.title: RTL cone & causal schematic graph

mcp_tools.description: Run svlang lint with the `formal-ready` rule pack (`SV-FPV-001..005`, SVA, CDC, FSM) on the elaborated design's RTL files and return findings with structured 1-click quick-fix byte edits.
mcp_tools.name: formal_lint
mcp_tools.title: Formal-readiness lint & quick-fixes

mcp_tools.description: Apply a byte-range quick-fix from `formal_lint` to a design file under the workspace root and re-elaborate (or record as a proposal in propose mode).
mcp_tools.name: formal_fix_apply
mcp_tools.title: Apply a formal-readiness quick-fix

mcp_tools.description: Resolve declarations, sequential/combinational drivers, and SVA/expression loads of an RTL signal across the design's files.
mcp_tools.name: signal_nav
mcp_tools.title: Go-to-driver and go-to-load navigation

mcp_tools.description: Analyze COI state bits, arithmetic operators, memories, and blackbox candidates (`get_fv_complexity`) for a property or the whole task.
mcp_tools.name: fv_complexity
mcp_tools.title: Formal complexity & hotspot report

mcp_tools.description: Cross-check the active session against a machine-verifiable formal verification spec (`fvp.spec.json` / `informal.spec/1`): verifies design/clock/reset intent, legal primary-input-only assumption boundary, per-requirement assertion + witness-cover status (`verified`, `cex`, `undetermined`, `missing_assert`, `missing_cover`, `vacuous`, `overconstrained`), signoff gates, and prioritized next actions. Auto-discovers `fvp.spec.json` next to the design files when `spec_file` and `spec` are omitted.
mcp_tools.name: spec_audit
mcp_tools.title: Audit session against fvp.spec.json

mcp_tools.description: The escape hatch: evaluate a JasperGold or VC Formal style command in the session's shell. In automatic mode it runs; in propose mode it is recorded as a proposal that waits for a person (give `rationale`). Prefer the other tools: their replies are data.
mcp_tools.name: tcl_eval
mcp_tools.title: Evaluate a Tcl command

mcp_tools.description: The window of the person working on this session: the property they selected, the view and layout preset, the open trace with their cursor's frame, callouts and signals, the source lines in view, schematic state, and any @-focus pills.
mcp_tools.name: gui_state
mcp_tools.title: What the person is looking at

mcp_tools.description: Select a property in the person's property table, as a click would: its details and source line show.
mcp_tools.name: gui_select_property
mcp_tools.title: Select a property in the window

mcp_tools.description: Open the waveform of a property whose status is cex or covered in the person's window, with the cursor on `frame` (default: the frame where it fails or is hit). Use it to show the person the cycle you are talking about.
mcp_tools.name: gui_open_trace
mcp_tools.title: Open a trace in the window

mcp_tools.description: Add signals, by full name as trace_get gives them, to the waveform that is open in the person's window. Fails when no trace is open or a signal is not in that trace.
mcp_tools.name: gui_add_signals
mcp_tools.title: Add signals to the open waveform

mcp_tools.description: Open a design file or script in the person's source view and highlight a range of lines.
mcp_tools.name: gui_highlight_source
mcp_tools.title: Show source lines in the window

mcp_tools.description: Switch the centre view (`table`, `source`, `trace`, `schematic`, `apps`), workspace layout preset (`triage`, `cex-debug`, `signoff`, `split`), Formal App tab (`cov`, `xprop`, `spv`, `sec`, `csr`, `protocol`), bottom dock tab, or property filter.
mcp_tools.name: gui_set_view
mcp_tools.title: Switch window view, layout preset, dock tab, or filter

mcp_tools.description: Open or close the `Why CEX` backward causal slice overlay on the open waveform, and optionally filter lanes to causal signals only (`slice_only`).
mcp_tools.name: gui_toggle_why_cex
mcp_tools.title: Toggle Why CEX causal root-cause slice overlay

mcp_tools.description: Pin visual callout badges onto specific `(signal, frame)` cells in the open waveform (or clear them) so the engineer sees exact root-cause transitions.
mcp_tools.name: gui_annotate_trace
mcp_tools.title: Pin AI callout badges onto waveform cells

mcp_tools.description: Publish, step, or dismiss an interactive multi-step root-cause tour bar in the window that synchronizes the waveform cursor, callout pins, and RTL source lines on each step.
mcp_tools.name: gui_present_walkthrough
mcp_tools.title: Present or step a guided multi-step CEX walkthrough

mcp_tools.description: Open the schematic viewer for property `name` (default: selected property) at `max_depth` register stages.
mcp_tools.name: gui_open_schematic
mcp_tools.title: Open the interactive COI & causal schematic

mcp_tools.description: Preferred single-call desktop visual tour for a `cex` or `covered` property: switches to `cex-debug` (or chosen layout preset), opens the trace at `frame`, activates the `Why CEX` causal slice, pins AI callout badges, and launches the interactive walkthrough bar. Auto-synthesizes steps and callouts from `why_cex` when omitted.
mcp_tools.name: gui_present_cex
mcp_tools.title: Atomically present a synchronized CEX debug walkthrough

mcp_tools.description: Render a standalone SVG of the open waveform or schematic (including Why CEX highlights and AI callout badges) into `window.capture` for visual verification or Markdown reports.
mcp_tools.name: gui_capture_view
mcp_tools.title: Capture deterministic SVG or visual summary of the active view

tcl_commands.name: help
tcl_commands.notes: Use `jg::<cmd>` or `vcf::<cmd>` to disambiguate commands that exist in both flavors (such as `analyze` or `elaborate`).

options.desc: List commands across common, JasperGold (jg), and VC Formal (vcf) flavors
List VC Formal-flavor and common commands
Show full detail for a command (accepted for vendor compatibility)
Emit the full command catalog as JSON

tcl_commands.summary: Show Tcl command reference, options, and examples

tcl_commands.name: get_version
tcl_commands.summary: Return the InFormal version string

tcl_commands.name: echo
tcl_commands.notes: Suppressed in `informal shell --check` dry-run mode.
tcl_commands.summary: Print arguments separated by spaces to standard output

tcl_commands.name: session
tcl_commands.notes: Useful for debugging scripts or driving external tooling.
tcl_commands.summary: Dump the complete FPV session state as pretty-printed JSON

tcl_commands.name: set_lowering
tcl_commands.notes: Both switches default to `off` (decision D13: never guess silently). Changing a switch invalidates elaboration so the next `elaborate` or `prove` re-lowers.

options.desc: Omit time-0 checks in `initial` blocks instead of rejecting them
Lower `$isunknown(x)` as constant `0` (2-state) instead of rejecting it

tcl_commands.summary: Toggle opt-in SystemVerilog lowering relaxations

tcl_commands.name: check_assumptions
tcl_commands.notes: With `-dead_end`, returns `alive` or `dead_end at step ...`; with `-conflict`, returns a list of conflicting assumptions; otherwise returns the allowed trace depth. Automatically run before `prove` when vacuity checking is on.

options.desc: Unrolling depth for environment consistency check (default 20)
Compute a minimal conflicting subset of assumptions when overconstrained
Run 2QBF trap-state check detecting reachable states with no legal next input

tcl_commands.summary: Check assumption satisfiability, UNSAT conflict cores, and 2QBF dead-end trap states

tcl_commands.name: set_vacuity
tcl_commands.notes: On by default. Call with no arguments to query current state.

options.desc: Enable environment consistency (depth 20) and precondition vacuity covers

tcl_commands.summary: Enable or disable automatic environment and precondition vacuity checks

tcl_commands.name: set_engines
tcl_commands.notes: Pass an empty list to re-enable all configured engines. Unknown engine names are rejected with the available list.
tcl_commands.summary: Restrict the proof portfolio to named engines

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_cache
tcl_commands.notes: Keys are computed from the exact lowered Btor2 model (design + active assumptions + cut points + property).

options.desc: Enable caching of proven and unreachable verdicts
Disable proof cache lookup and writes

tcl_commands.summary: Enable or disable the content-addressed SHA-256 proof cache

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_cache_path
tcl_commands.notes: Share across CI runs to skip re-proving unchanged properties.
tcl_commands.summary: Get or set the proof cache directory path

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_cache_mode

options.desc: Read hits and store new proofs (default)
Reuse cached verdicts without writing new entries
Always re-prove and refresh cache entries

tcl_commands.summary: Set proof cache read/write policy

tcl_commands.name: check_conn
tcl_commands.notes: Supports `CONNECTION,name,src,dst`, `CONDITION,name,cond`, and `LATENCY,name,cycles` CSV directives.

options.desc: Load OpenTitan/JasperGold CONNECTION/CONDITION/LATENCY CSV into task
Print connectivity verification summary (use `-file F [-force]` to save)
Write report to file (with `-force` to overwrite)

tcl_commands.summary: Formal Connectivity App: verify pin-to-pin / muxed / pipelined CSV connectivity maps

tcl_commands.name: check_cov
tcl_commands.notes: Proves unreachable branches/toggles (UNR) and reports Cone-of-Influence observability.

options.desc: Initialize coverage models (`-model {coi branch toggle functional}`)
Run formal reachability/COI measurement on active cover items
Print coverage summary (`-html -report_file F -force` for HTML report)
Restrict measurement or reporting to specific task(s)

tcl_commands.summary: Formal Coverage & UNR App: COI observability, branch/toggle dead-code detection, and waivers

tcl_commands.name: check_xprop
tcl_commands.notes: Uses exact 2-copy self-composition (avoiding false mux X-pessimism).

options.desc: Observation targets: `outputs`, `flops`, `all`, or explicit signal list
X injection sources: reset-less flops, X literals, undriven nets
Explicit target signals to check for X reachability

tcl_commands.summary: Exact 2-copy self-composition Formal X-Propagation App

tcl_commands.name: check_spv
tcl_commands.notes: Detects both direct combinational and multi-cycle covert storage leaks via 2-copy miter.

options.desc: Define a taint/isolation check (`-name N -from S -to O [-cond C]`)
Property name for the security path check
Sensitive source signal (e.g., key register or port)
Observable sink signal (e.g., public or debug output)
Optional guard condition under which isolation must hold

tcl_commands.summary: Formal Security Path Verification (SPV) App: 2-safety non-interference and taint flow

tcl_commands.name: check_sec
tcl_commands.notes: Generates side-by-side `spec`/`imp` mismatch VCD traces on non-equivalence.

options.desc: Run combinational keypoint equivalence mode (match state/outputs directly)
Retiming pipeline latency offset (`imp` delayed by N cycles relative to `spec`)
Clock and reset expression for sequential equivalence
Explicitly map `-input`, `-output`, `-state`, or `-output_latency` pairs, or add `-assume`
Prove equivalence across all mapped outputs

tcl_commands.summary: Formal Sequential (SEC) and Combinational (LEC) Equivalence Checking App

tcl_commands.name: check_csr
tcl_commands.notes: Auto-infers standard bus port names (`addr`, `we`, `re`, `wdata`, `rdata`) unless overridden.

options.desc: Load register spec (`.hjson`, `.csv`, or `uvm_reg_block` `.sv`) and generate checks
Prove all generated CSR reset, access (`RW`/`RO`/`W1C`/`W1S`/`W0C`/`WO`/`RC`), `regwen`, and non-aliasing checks

tcl_commands.summary: Formal CSR / RAL Verification App from OpenTitan HJSON, CSV, or UVM RAL `.sv`

tcl_commands.name: check_protocol
tcl_commands.notes: Generates both protocol safety assertions and legal bus master/slave environment assumptions matched to `-role`.

options.desc: DUT role: `slave` (assert responses, assume requests), `master`, or `monitor`
Optional signal name prefix on the top module
Instance label for generated protocol properties

tcl_commands.summary: 1-command Formal Bus Protocol VIP Generator (`tlul`, `axi4lite`, `apb`)

tcl_commands.equivalent: JasperGold Visualize QuietTrace / VC Formal RCA
tcl_commands.name: why_cex
tcl_commands.notes: Walks backward from failure cycle T to 0, pruning untaken mux arms and non-controlling logic operands.

options.desc: Failing assertion or covered witness property name

tcl_commands.summary: Compute a dynamic backward causal root-cause slice of a CEX or cover trace

tcl_commands.name: get_fv_complexity
tcl_commands.notes: Highlights wide counters, multipliers, and unpacked arrays that stall bit-level IC3/k-induction.

options.desc: Restrict complexity analysis to one property's COI

tcl_commands.summary: Analyze cone-of-influence state bits, memories, and wide-arithmetic proof hotspots

tcl_commands.name: blackbox_assistant
tcl_commands.notes: Run before `prove` or when `get_fv_complexity` flags deep arithmetic/storage blocks.

options.desc: Minimum flop/memory bit threshold to flag a candidate
Automatically add recommended modules to the blackbox list

tcl_commands.summary: Recommend or apply complexity-driven black-boxing of heavy submodules

tcl_commands.name: check_fv_setup

options.desc: Include detailed signal lists for each finding
Write setup report to file (`-force` to overwrite)

tcl_commands.summary: Audit formal setup completeness (clocks, resets, reset-less flops, undriven nets, abstractions)

tcl_commands.name: report_fv_setup

options.desc: Write setup report to file (`-force` to overwrite)

tcl_commands.summary: Alias for `check_fv_setup`: report formal setup audit findings

tcl_commands.name: get_reset_info
tcl_commands.summary: Report declared reset expression, async resets found, and reset-less registers

tcl_commands.name: abstract

options.desc: Apply abstraction to a specific task

tcl_commands.summary: Apply sound over-approximate counter jump abstractions to accelerate deep proofs
tcl_commands.usage: abstract -counter <sig> [-threshold K] [-init_value V] [-task T] | abstract -list | abstract -clear

tcl_commands.name: report_abstractions
tcl_commands.summary: List active formal abstractions and their parameters

tcl_commands.name: set_abstractions
tcl_commands.summary: Clear or disable active formal abstractions

tcl_commands.name: clear

options.desc: Clear all design state, tasks, and properties

tcl_commands.summary: Reset the current session, clearing design files, elaboration, and properties

tcl_commands.name: analyze
tcl_commands.notes: VHDL (`-vhdl*`) is rejected with a clear error.

options.desc: Language standard flags (accepted; parsed as IEEE 1800-2023 SystemVerilog)
Mark module name(s) as source-less black boxes
Clear previously analyzed files and black boxes
Read compile arguments and files from a VCS/Jasper filelist (`$VAR` expanded)

tcl_commands.summary: Collect SystemVerilog source files, filelists, defines, and include paths

tcl_commands.name: elaborate
tcl_commands.notes: Extracts all RTL concurrent and immediate assertions, assumptions, and covers into `<embedded>`.

options.desc: Top module name (inferred if omitted and unambiguous)
Black-box module definition(s) (outputs become free inputs)
Auto-blackbox multipliers at or above `<bits>` width
Auto-blackbox unpacked arrays/memories at or above `<words>` depth

tcl_commands.summary: Elaborate the analyzed SystemVerilog design with `svlang`
tcl_commands.usage: elaborate [-top M] [-parameter P V] [-bbox_m {M ...}] [-bbox_i {inst ...}] [-bbox_mul W] [-bbox_a N] [-disable_auto_bbox] [-no_preconditions] [-create_related_covers {precondition witness}]

tcl_commands.name: clock
tcl_commands.notes: Tcl's standard `clock seconds` / `clock format` subcommands are automatically forwarded to `::informal::tcl_clock`.

options.desc: Clock period multiplier relative to the primary clock
Accepted for compatibility (both edges handled by netlist)
Auto-infer clocks from elaborated sequential elements

tcl_commands.summary: Declare primary or derived design clocks (or forward Tcl's built-in `clock`)
tcl_commands.usage: clock <sig> [-factor N] [-phase P] [-both_edges] | clock -clear | clock -none | clock -infer

tcl_commands.name: reset
tcl_commands.notes: Expression identifiers are checked against the elaborated top module.

options.desc: Active-high reset predicate (e.g., `{!rst_n}` for active-low reset)
Run without an explicit reset constraint
Report reset structure without changing the session reset

tcl_commands.summary: Declare the formal reset condition held in cycle 0 and released thereafter

tcl_commands.name: assert
tcl_commands.notes: Identifiers are validated against top-module declarations immediately; unsupported SVA operators report cleanly on `prove`.

options.desc: Cap proof depth at `K` cycles (reports `bounded_proven` if unviolated)
Treat this property as an environment `assume` instead of an assertion
Toggle or delete matching properties (glob or `-regexp`)
Interpret selection pattern as a regular expression

tcl_commands.summary: Add, enable, disable, or remove SVA assertions in a task
tcl_commands.usage: assert [-name N] [-task T] [-bound K] [-env] {<sva_expr>} | assert (-disable|-enable|-remove) [-task T] [-regexp] <pattern ...>

tcl_commands.name: assume
tcl_commands.notes: `-from_assert` never circularly assumes assertion P while proving P itself.

options.desc: Promote helper assertion(s) into assumptions with provenance tracking
Toggle or delete matching assumptions (including RTL assumes per task)
Interpret pattern as a regular expression

tcl_commands.summary: Add environment assumptions, promote helper assertions, or toggle/remove assumptions
tcl_commands.usage: assume [-name N] [-task T] {<sva_expr>} | assume -from_assert <pat> [-name N] [-task T] [-regexp] | assume (-disable|-enable|-remove) [-task T] [-regexp] <pattern ...>

tcl_commands.name: cover
tcl_commands.notes: A witness trace proves reachability (`covered`); an unbounded safety proof means `unreachable`.

options.desc: Interpret selection pattern as a regular expression

tcl_commands.summary: Add, enable, disable, or remove SVA reachability cover properties
tcl_commands.usage: cover [-name N] [-task T] [-bound K] {<sva_expr>} | cover (-disable|-enable|-remove) [-task T] [-regexp] <pattern ...>

tcl_commands.name: prove
tcl_commands.notes: Runs environment consistency check first (when vacuity is on), sweeps multi-property tasks at `low` effort before converging undetermined targets, and runs precondition/witness covers after proven assertions.

options.desc: Prove all enabled properties in the current task
Prove all enabled properties in task `T`
Prove only the named property or properties
Cap whole-batch wall-clock time across all targets (`0`/`off` disables)
Extract minimal needed assumptions and state support for proven assertions

tcl_commands.summary: Run the engine portfolio on properties or tasks and print a verdict table
tcl_commands.usage: prove [-all] [-task T] [-property {P ...}] [-effort low|standard|high|max] [-orchestration auto|on|off] [-time_limit D] [-total_time_limit D] [-bound K] [-with_proof_core]

tcl_commands.name: get_property_list
tcl_commands.notes: Returns a Tcl list of matching property names.

options.desc: Treat `name` filter values as regular expressions

tcl_commands.summary: Query property names filtered by type, status, task, name, or disabled flag

tcl_commands.name: get_status
tcl_commands.notes: Returns one of `proven`, `bounded_proven`, `cex`, `covered`, `unreachable`, `undetermined`, `error`, or `unprocessed`.
tcl_commands.summary: Return the verification status string of a single property

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_time_limit
tcl_commands.notes: Accepts durations with `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d` suffixes.
tcl_commands.summary: Set the session default per-property proof time limit

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_per_property_time_limit
tcl_commands.summary: Set the per-property proof time limit (alias for `set_prove_time_limit`)

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_total_time_limit
tcl_commands.notes: Pass `0` or `off` to clear the batch cap; call with no arguments to query the current setting.
tcl_commands.summary: Set or query the whole-batch wall-clock time limit across a `prove` run

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_effort
tcl_commands.notes: Call with no arguments to return the current effort level.

options.desc: Skip `scorr` & simulation mining; run lightweight 1-step BMC/k-ind/IC3 subset
Enable simulation + Houdini 2-literal mining, deeper CTG (`8`/`3`), derived predicates, and IC3 slice restarts
`high` plus 6-worker diverse `Ic3Mt` pool and automatic witness cover + minimal proof-core signoff

tcl_commands.summary: Set or query the session engine proof effort level (`low`, `standard`, `high`, `max`)

tcl_commands.name: set_prove_orchestration
tcl_commands.notes: Pass 1 sweeps targets for `min(2s, max(250ms, time_limit / 10))` at `low` effort so easy properties settle immediately before Pass 2 focuses full effort on remaining undetermined targets.

options.desc: Enable two-pass sweep/converge automatically on multi-property runs (default)
Always run a fast `low`-effort sweep pass before full-effort convergence
Run every property in a single pass at the configured effort

tcl_commands.summary: Set or query two-pass proof orchestration (`auto`, `on`, `off`)

tcl_commands.name: set_engine_mode
tcl_commands.notes: Maps `Ht`/`Hp` -> IC3/PDR, `B` -> BMC, `N` -> portfolio and prints the selected engines.
tcl_commands.summary: Map JasperGold engine mode letters (`Ht`, `Hp`, `B`, `N`, ...) to InFormal engines

tcl_commands.name: report

options.desc: Print detailed per-property engine, depth, vacuity, and memory metrics
Print design structure and lowered model sizes (`get_design_info`)
Write output to file (`-force` overwrites existing file)

tcl_commands.summary: Print or export property tables, CSV summaries, design info, or per-property details

tcl_commands.name: get_design_info
tcl_commands.notes: Reports exact counts from `svlang` netlist plus the current task's Btor2 and AIG sizes.

options.desc: Return Tcl list of `instance`, `memory`, `clock`, or `reset` names

tcl_commands.summary: Inspect elaborated design counts (flops, latches, memories, clocks) and model sizes

tcl_commands.name: get_property_info

options.desc: Include inputs and registers in the property's cone of influence

tcl_commands.summary: Inspect one property's status, engine stats, COI cone, or minimal proof core

tcl_commands.name: get_stats
tcl_commands.summary: Return per-property proof statistics (engine, wall/CPU time, depth, peak memory) as JSON

tcl_commands.name: stopat
tcl_commands.notes: Cut points are task-scoped: cutting a signal in task `T` leaves it driven in `<embedded>` and other tasks.

options.desc: Apply cut points to task `T` (default current task)
Remove listed cut points, or all cut points in the task
Return active cut points as a Tcl list

tcl_commands.summary: Cut signals from their RTL drivers so they become unconstrained free inputs in a task
tcl_commands.usage: stopat [-task T] <sig ...> | stopat -clear [-task T] [sig ...] | stopat -list [-task T]

tcl_commands.name: task
tcl_commands.notes: Call `task` with no arguments to return the current task name. Each task is lowered and proved independently.

options.desc: Create task `T` (optionally with `-set` and copy flags)
Copy additional properties or cut points into existing task `T`
Return Tcl list of task names (`<embedded>` first)
Copy all properties of the specified kind
Copy cut points, or copy all properties and cut points

tcl_commands.summary: Create, edit, switch, list, or delete isolated formal verification tasks
tcl_commands.usage: task [-create T|-edit T|-set T|-delete T|-list] [-source_task S] [-copy {pat}] [-copy_asserts] [-copy_assumes] [-copy_covers] [-copy_stopats] [-copy_all] [-regexp]

tcl_commands.name: get_task_list
tcl_commands.summary: Return the Tcl list of all tasks in the session

tcl_commands.name: visualize
tcl_commands.notes: If `$INFORMAL_WAVE_VIEWER` (e.g., `surfer` or `gtkwave`) is set, spawns the viewer on the VCD file.

options.desc: Open the counterexample trace for a failing assertion
Open the witness trace for a covered property

tcl_commands.summary: Return the VCD trace path for a CEX or cover and optionally launch `$INFORMAL_WAVE_VIEWER`

tcl_commands.name: include
tcl_commands.notes: Followed recursively by `informal shell --check`.
tcl_commands.summary: Source another Tcl file in the global scope (JasperGold alias for `source`)

tcl_commands.name: set_proofgrid_per_engine_max_jobs
tcl_commands.notes: Accepted so existing JasperGold setup scripts run unmodified.
tcl_commands.summary: Vendor proof-grid tuning command (accepted and ignored with a note)

tcl_commands.name: set_proofgrid_per_engine_max_local_jobs
tcl_commands.notes: Accepted so existing JasperGold setup scripts run unmodified.
tcl_commands.summary: Vendor proof-grid tuning command (accepted and ignored with a note)

tcl_commands.name: set_proofgrid_max_local_jobs
tcl_commands.notes: Accepted so existing JasperGold setup scripts run unmodified.
tcl_commands.summary: Vendor proof-grid tuning command (accepted and ignored with a note)

tcl_commands.name: set_proofgrid_max_jobs
tcl_commands.notes: Accepted so existing JasperGold setup scripts run unmodified.
tcl_commands.summary: Vendor proof-grid tuning command (accepted and ignored with a note)

tcl_commands.name: set_proofgrid_mode
tcl_commands.notes: Accepted so existing JasperGold setup scripts run unmodified.
tcl_commands.summary: Vendor proof-grid mode command (accepted and ignored with a note)

tcl_commands.name: set_max_trace_length
tcl_commands.notes: Caps `informal-bmc` / `informal-wbmc` depth while still allowing inductive engines (`kind`, `ic3`, `wkind`) to prove unboundedly (`proven`, `∞`). Assertions cleared cleanly to bound `N` without an unbounded proof report `bounded_proven`.
tcl_commands.summary: Set or query the persistent BMC unrolling bound (`0`/`off` clears)

tcl_commands.name: set_blackbox
tcl_commands.notes: Takes effect at the next `elaborate` or `read_file`.
tcl_commands.summary: Mark modules or cell instances as black boxes before elaboration

tcl_commands.name: set_fml_appmode
tcl_commands.notes: Currently accepts `FPV`; for Formal Apps (`check_cov`, `check_csr`, etc.) call the `check_*` commands directly.
tcl_commands.summary: Select VC Formal application mode (`FPV`)

tcl_commands.name: set_fml_var
tcl_commands.notes: Unknown vendor tuning variables are accepted and ignored with a note.

options.desc: Persistent BMC trace bound (`N`, or `0`/`off` to clear)

tcl_commands.summary: Set VC Formal session variable (`fml_max_time`, `fml_effort`, `fml_max_depth`)

tcl_commands.name: read_file
tcl_commands.summary: Analyze and elaborate SystemVerilog sources in one command

tcl_commands.name: analyze
tcl_commands.summary: Analyze SystemVerilog source files in VC Formal style

tcl_commands.name: elaborate

tcl_commands.name: create_clock

options.desc: Clock period (used for relative clock ratios)

tcl_commands.summary: Declare a design clock signal in VC Formal style

tcl_commands.name: create_reset

tcl_commands.name: sim_save_reset

options.desc: Prove only the specified property names
Override proof effort for this run (`low`, `standard`, `high`, `max`)
Override per-property timeout for this run

options.desc: Print detailed engine and vacuity statistics
Restrict verbose output to one property
